name: Lust and Pornography

counsel.text: Set faith at work on Christ for the killing of thy sin. His blood is the great sovereign remedy for sin-sick souls. Live in this, and thou wilt die a conqueror; yea, thou wilt, through the good providence of God, live to see thy lust dead at thy feet.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 14

counsel.text: Sin aims always at the utmost; every time it rises up to tempt or entice, might it have its own course, it would go out to the utmost sin in that kind. Every unclean thought or glance would be adultery if it could; every covetous desire would be oppression, every thought of unbelief would be atheism, might it grow to its head.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 2

counsel.text: Know that he that dares to dally with occasions of sin will dare to sin. He that will venture upon temptations unto wickedness will venture upon wickedness.
counsel.author: John Owen
counsel.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

counsel.text: For the provision to be laid up, it is that which is provided in the gospel for us. Gospel provisions will do this work; that is, keep the heart full of a sense of the love of God in Christ. This is the greatest preservative against the power of temptation in the world.
counsel.author: John Owen

counsel.text: The eye tempts the fancy, and the fancy works upon the heart. A wanton amorous eye may usher in sin. Eve first saw the tree of knowledge, and then she took. Gen 3: 6. First she looked and then she loved.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

counsel.text: To lascivious books I may add lascivious pictures, which bewitch the eye, and are incendiaries to lust. They secretly convey poison to the heart.
counsel.author: Thomas Watson
counsel.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

prayers.title: A prayer of confession
prayers.text: Holy Father, your eyes are too pure to look on evil, and nothing in me is hidden from you. I come to you only through Jesus Christ, your Son. I confess that I have sinned against you with my eyes, my thoughts, and my body. I have looked where I should have turned away. I have fed desires you forbid, and I have treated another person, made in your image, as a thing for my pleasure. Against you, you only, have I sinned. I have grieved your Holy Spirit and dishonored the body that belongs to you. I have no plea in myself. But Christ bore this very sin in his body on the tree, and his blood cleanses from all sin. He lives to intercede for me. For his sake, forgive me and wash me. Create in me a clean heart, O God, and renew a right spirit within me. By your Spirit put this lust to death at its root, and give me a greater delight in you than in any pleasure of sin. Keep me from ever calling this small again. I thank you that there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. In his name I pray. Amen.

prayers.title: In the hour of temptation
prayers.text: Lord Jesus, you were tempted in every way as I am, yet without sin, and you know how fierce this hour is. I will not hide it from you. Help me now. Turn my eyes from worthless things, and give me strength to get up and go. Remind me that my body is a temple of the Holy Spirit, and that I was bought with a price, your own blood. Show me again the joy that is in you, greater than this passing pleasure. Spirit of God, by your power put to death what is rising in me, and make a way of escape that I will take. I belong to you. Amen.

prayers.title: For a pure heart
prayers.text: Father, you have promised that the pure in heart shall see you. I want that blessing more than anything this world offers. Make my heart pure. Fill my mind with what is true, honorable, and lovely, so that there is no room left for what defiles. Teach me to see every man and woman as your image bearer, to honor them and never to use them. Guard my eyes, my hands, and my hours alone. Make me watchful over the occasions of sin, and quick to bring them into the light before my brethren. Above all, satisfy me with your steadfast love, so that I do not hunger for counterfeits. Through Jesus Christ my Lord. Amen.

examinationQuestions: When this desire stirred today, what were you seeking in it that you were not seeking from Christ: comfort, escape, rest, or to feel wanted?
What occasions of sin did you allow, such as a place, an hour, a device, or a thought you let linger, and where did you first turn toward it?
Do you grieve over this sin because it offends God and grieves his Spirit, or mostly because of the shame it brings you?
What does this sin whisper to you about God: that he does not see, or that he is keeping some good thing from you?
Have you thought of the people on the screen as someone's son or daughter, made in God's image and needing Christ, or only as things to use?
Have you brought this sin into the light with one of your brethren or your pastor, or are you still keeping it in the dark?
fleeActions: Put the phone or computer down now. Leave it in another room, and do not go back to it for at least an hour.
Get up and leave the place where you are. Go where other people are, or step outside and walk, and then take up the next duty in front of you.
Text or call one of your brethren now. Say plainly, "I am being tempted. Please pray for me."
Open a paper Bible, not a screen, and read Psalm 51 or Psalm 119:9-16 out loud.
If it is late, go to bed now. Leave every screen outside the room, and pray before you lie down.
Today, put a filter and accountability on every device you use, and give the passwords to someone you trust in your church.

afterFallReadings.text: Hast thou not often been ready to conclude thyself, that it was utterly impossible that he should bear any longer with thee; that he would cast thee off, and be gracious no more; that all his forbearance was exhausted, and hell and wrath was even ready prepared for thee? and yet, above all thy expectation, he hath returned with visitations of love.
afterFallReadings.author: John Owen
afterFallReadings.source: Of the Mortification of Sin in Believers, ch. 11

afterFallReadings.text: A soul steeped in the briny tears of repentance, and bathed in the blood of Christ, is made pure.
afterFallReadings.author: Thomas Watson
afterFallReadings.source: The Ten Commandments, the seventh commandment

afterFallReadings.text: I also saw, moreover, that it was not my good frame of heart that made my righteousness better, nor yet my bad frame that made my righteousness worse; for my righteousness was Jesus Christ Himself, the same yesterday, and to-day, and for ever (Heb. 13.8).
afterFallReadings.author: John Bunyan
afterFallReadings.source: Grace Abounding to the Chief of Sinners, §229
